newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt gains from strong U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt gains from strong U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Emerging debt prices rose Tuesday on continued strength spilling over from the U.S. Treasury market economy, traders said.

The debt markets prospered after a report on U.S. wages, the Employment Cost Index, rose only 0.8 percent in the second quarter of 1997 and soothed fears that tight U.S. labor conditions were pushing through to inflation.
"We're seeing new highs because of the Treasuries," one Brady bond trader said. "We didn't see any customer business."
While the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond climbed 8/32 to yield 6.39 percent, Brazilian "C" bonds gained 3/8 to a bid price of 84 and Mexican Discounts edged up 1/4 to 95.
The overall Brady market approached its record spread to U.S. Treasuries, tightening another few basis points to around 370 over, dealers said.
"There was not a whole lot of activity but there was some tightening," Tulio Vera, managing director at Bear Stearns. "The Brady spread is close to its record again."
Raul Elizalde, global fixed income strategist at ING Barings, forecast narrower spreads, but said these gains could not go on forever.
"After some more spread compression thee is not that much more we can expect," Elizalde said. "A lot of the juice is being squeezed out of the market."
Vera said the market could continue its gradual firming, tightening another 25-50 basis points before the rally runs out of steam.

"The gradual trend in most countries is continued improvements in credit worthiness, and the brackdrop in the U.S., after (Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan's testimony, is very encouraging," Vera said.
